depth_findings.text: Capability-core sweeper inserts fire_key unconditionally; against a database without migration 0056 the insert fails. Flag-off is not byte-identical at the DB level until the migration ships first.

The receipt RPC does not check run status, so with the switch on an early-return failed step for a cancelled run settles its fire to failed. This is the intended behaviour but is untested against a real cancelled run.
With the switch on, ZDR runs also settle fire status through the receipt RPC (numeric and status only, no content). Control refuses ZDR scheduled runs upstream, so this path should not be reached.
No DB test covers the receipt-settled fire for a completed step with the EC flag off and SC flag on (receipt-only completed path).
RecordScheduledRunResult persists withheld_effects but not rounds_executed, tool_calls, input_tokens or output_tokens, which the plan's S6 cost rows need.
The fires listing is org-scoped with an existence check, but the plan's S3 row says creator-scoped. Either the plan or the handler needs a decision.
The Space session should confirm the audience predicate treats origin=schedule threads as non-extractable (plan cross-session note).

The capability-core sweeper now inserts cron_fires.fire_key unconditionally (sweeper.go fireOne, both INSERT INTO cron_fires statements), so against a database without migration 0056 every fire insert fails and schedules stop firing; flag-off is therefore not identical at the DB level. The lead must gate the rollout: session-core migration 0056 applied before capability-core starts this sweeper.

The code comment in session-core grpc.rs (append_scheduled_result_in_tx) says a scheduled answer runs no memory extraction, but dreaming.rs load_pending_messages only skips threads with source_scope = 'conversation' (about line 223 and 1268), and a scheduled thread keeps the default 'workspace', so its answer is picked up for extraction; the Dreaming predicate in K3-5 must exclude origin 'space' schedule threads, or the comment must be corrected, before SESSION_CORE_SCHEDULED_RESULT_PERSIST is turned on.

GET /api/v1/cron/{id}/fires is org-scoped (listFires checks only cron_schedules id and org_id), so any org member can list another member's schedule fires with run_id and thread_id; the S1 row asks for creator-scoping 'like get :995', but get itself is org-scoped (workplane_apis.go about line 1076), so the row and the code disagree and the owner must decide before S3 shows the listing.

The plan-named execution-core test scheduled_step_persists_output_through_session_core is absent; the new execution-core tests only cover the request builder and the switch parse, so the EC flag-on branch (record_scheduled_run_result call and its error mapping) has no test.

scripts/tests/scheduled-step-receipt-postgres-test.sh (not owned) runs only scheduled_step_claim_and_unknown_receipt_are_idempotent_against_real_pg, so the three new DB tests (record_scheduled_run_result_appends_once_and_completes_receipt, record_scheduled_run_result_refuses_zdr_run, record_scheduled_step_receipt_settles_failed_and_unknown_fires) never run through the plan's named command; the lead should add run_session_test lines for them.

No test covers settle_scheduled_fire in terminalization.rs, the terminal-run path that sets fire status from the run outcome when the switch is on, and no DB test covers a completed receipt-settled fire with the EC flag off and the SC flag on.

Appendix B.1 note N2 requires the proto-tag additivity proof (a diff of tag numbers against git show HEAD of sessions.proto) to be attached to this slice; the implementer did not attach it, and it can be produced from the 36-line diff, which only adds the RPC and two messages at tags 1-14 and 1-3.

RecordScheduledRunResult persists only output and withheld_effects; rounds_executed, tool_calls, input_tokens and output_tokens are accepted and dropped, which the plan's S6 cost rows will need. The proto comment documents this, so it is a tracked gap, not a defect here.

With the SC switch on, the receipt RPC settles fires for ZDR runs too (numeric and status only, as the plan allows), and a completed step with the EC flag off settles its fire to completed with no answer stored; both are intended but should be stated in ZDR.md when that doc is updated.
The 0056 migration header says the writes are gated by SESSION_CORE_SCHEDULED_RESULT_PERSIST, but the sweeper's fire_key insert is not gated; the comment is inaccurate.
